criteria.semantics: A native <nav> landmark named by the nav's label (aria-label), its links in a native <ul>, one <li> each.

keyboard.outcome: Moves through the nav's links in order.

keyboard.key: Screen reader landmark keys (D, the rotor)
keyboard.outcome: Move to the nav by its name.

criteria.name: The nav's label.
criteria.role: Navigation landmark, and a list of its links.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the links grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the links stack or wrap, none cut off, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <nav> element.
The nav is named by its label in aria-label, so two navs on a page are told apart.
Its links are a native list: a <ul> with one <li> per link.
WHEN I list the landmarks with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR the nav by its name and the role of navigation.
WHEN I Tab into the nav I HEAR the list and how many links it has.

criteria.semantics: The nav's label, then its links, each a stop in the tab order; the nav itself is not. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Navigation landmark named by its label, its links a list.

keyboard.outcome: Move through the nav's links in reading order.

criteria.name: The nav's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the label and the links grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the label and the links drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the label and the links at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the label and the links drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the label and the links whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A nav adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the nav's label above its links.
WHEN I move by landmarks with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR the nav by its name and the role of navigation.

announce.api: AXGroup with AXSubrole AXLandmarkNavigation, its label as the AXDescription (AccessKit Role::Navigation).
ControlType Group with LandmarkType Navigation, its label as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_LANDMARK with xml-roles navigation, its label as the name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
